# Doris K. Miller

Doris K. Miller (1919-1943) was an African American U.S. Navy sailor who became a national hero for his actions during the attack on Pearl Harbor.

## Pearl Harbor (December 7, 1941)

- Miller was a messman (a service role typically assigned to Black sailors) aboard the USS West Virginia
- During the Japanese attack, he manned a .50-caliber anti-aircraft gun despite having no formal combat training
- He is credited with shooting down multiple enemy aircraft during the assault
- His actions exemplified courage under fire and challenged racial stereotypes about Black military service

## Recognition and Legacy

- He was awarded the Navy Cross, making him the first Black recipient of this medal
- He received widespread media attention and became a symbol of Black heroism and patriotism
- He was promoted to petty officer third class

## Later Service and Death

- Miller continued serving in the Navy
- He was killed in action on November 24, 1943, when the USS Liscome Bay (an escort carrier where he was serving) was sunk by a Japanese submarine
- He was 24 years old

## Historical Significance

Miller's story helped challenge racial segregation in the military and demonstrated that Black Americans deserved equal opportunities and recognition. He remains an important figure in both naval history and the history of civil rights.
